content.title: How to watch 2026 NCAA basketball national championship game for free
content.text: The UConn Huskies are seeking their third national title in four seasons. Find out how to watch their battle with Michigan in the title game for free tonight. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comINDIANAPOLIS – The top-seeded Michigan Wolverines and the second-seeded UConn Huskies meet for the 2026 NCAA men’s basketball national championship today with the backdrop of the Indianapolis Colts’ Lucas Oil Stadium. You can watch this game for free. How do I watch Michigan vs. UConn for free? The 2026 NCAA Division I men’s college basketball national title game will broadcast at 8:49 p.m. Eastern on TBS and truTV. You can watch at no cost by utilizing a free trial and $35 off your first month from DIRECTV.SlingTV has promotional offers for new customers, including half off your first month. The cheapest way to watch this game is through the $4.99 day pass.Another way to watch on SlingTV is through the Orange and Blue package for just $29.99/month. Here are five storylines to watch for today’s game: 1. Michigan’s marries a record-breaking offense with a menacing defenseThe Wolverines (36-3) became the first team in NCAA history to score 90 or more points in five tournament games, bolstering a run defined by a 21.6-point average margin of victory. This offensive surge complements the nation’s best defense, which currently holds an 88.7 defensive rating and recently held Arizona to 37% shooting. Michigan is seeking its first title since 1989 and second in program history. 2. Star forward Yaxel Lendeborg’s health remains the game’s biggest uncertaintyMichigan’s leading scorer and rebounder, Yaxel Lendeborg, is recovering from MCL and ankle sprains suffered in the Final Four, leaving him potentially limited for the title game. However, junior center Aday Mara proved the team’s depth by exploding for 26 points and nine rebounds during Lendeborg’s absence in the previous round.3. UConn pursues rare dynasty status under Dan Hurley’s leadershipThe Huskies (34-5) are aiming for their third championship in four years, led by a head coach who has won 19 of his last 20 March Madness games. Senior forward Alex Karaban is currently 40 minutes away from securing his third individual national title, an achievement that would place him in rarified air within collegiate basketball history.4. Injury and shooting slumps threaten UConn’s offensive consistencyThe Huskies face a potential roster gap as junior guard Solo Ball was placed in a walking boot following a foot sprain, leaving his status for the final unclear. This injury coincides with a significant slump for Alex Karaban, who has shot just 3 of 18 from the field over his last two games.5. Free throw discipline and assist volume serve as the tactical battlegroundsUConn ranks near the bottom of the nation (307th) in preventing opponent free throw attempts, a vulnerability Michigan’s efficient shooters are well-positioned to exploit. Conversely, the Wolverines’ only three losses this season occurred when they allowed an opposing player to record six or more assists, providing a clear blueprint for the Huskies’ offense.Here’s more information on how to watch Michigan vs. UConn on TV and streaming services: What: 2026 NCAA Division I men’s basketball national championship game: Michigan vs. UConnWhen: Monday, April 6, 2026Time: 8:49 p.m. EasternChannel: TBS and truTVWhere: Lucas Oil Stadium | Indianapolis, Ind.
